cells.tense: Something a change left behind is in your hands, and you are turning it over.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: With what just came in, hand one thing over and accept one thing back in the same motion — a yes and a no, a hand out and a hand open. No clock on it; take the first moment it fits.
cells.core:
When something new arrives — a feeling, an offer, a version of a person — you let it land and stay still long enough to find out what it is before you decide what it's for. Time settles on it. You treat the plate on the counter the same way, which is why people leave calmer than they came.

The bend is that staying put is so calm the exchange has thinned. What comes in stays in, and the pair goes lopsided. So let the trade close. Hand one thing over and take one back in the same move. That could mean a yes before you're ready or a no before the other person has finished asking. Either way the pair balances. Nothing has to change about how long you take to know a thing; only that it goes back out, paired, at the first chance.
cells.sheetLine: The change settled into something. Now let it pass hands.
cells.verb: Holding what a change produced, in a shape that stands
cells.place: What is entering now, and how to meet it

cells.tense: You are bracing for what is going to come through the door next, and planning the meeting before it happens.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Before you sort what's arriving into a plan, let it pull you once — turn toward it, stay with it a minute, decide nothing.
cells.core:
What's arriving has a pull of its own. It doesn't often get to move you, because you've already pictured what's coming and picked a posture for it. The readiness is the trouble just now. It stands where the meeting should be, and the thing arriving finds someone already braced.

So go sideways. The next time something entering your life pulls at you, let the pull happen before you name it. Follow it a step. It may come to nothing. What you get is the pull itself, which is information you've been stepping past. When one of these arrivals turns out to be the real one, you'll already be turned toward it instead of facing the door.

cells.tense: A change finished, and you are still standing at the threshold, waiting to be let in.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: Next time something pushes against a direction you chose, stay where you put yourself — no arguing, no explaining. Just don't step off the spot.
cells.core:
Something you made has been finished for some time, and it's good. You haven't picked it up and carried it inside. New things keep arriving and you meet them from the threshold, hand still on the frame. The standing is old; the arrival is not.

What's coming in now needs no courage to receive. It needs a heading already chosen, held. The move is small: when you're pushed off something you committed to here, hold the line without a speech. Just don't step off the mark. Holding a heading once steadies everything behind it. You're carrying, not explaining. What was finished comes with you into the room, and the threshold stops mattering.

cells.tense: While you tell it as waiting on what's coming, some arrangement here is standing because of you.
cells.act: let the structure act instead of announcing it
cells.ask: Take one open question here that's already yours to settle. Settle it and carry it through the day without telling anyone why — let the doing speak in place of any word about it.
cells.core:
Something keeps producing quiet order here, and it holds because you hold it. Told from your side, that wouldn't come up. The version you tell has you watching the threshold for what's due to arrive.

The lift is to stop narrating. Settle one open thing that's already yours to settle, and carry it through without a word of explanation. Not a big one. The doing is the statement, and a doing doesn't need a reason told to anyone. Once it's done, the waiting story has nothing to stand on. Nothing was missing. The thing was only unnamed, and saying the name was not the job.
